AMEND SECTION 221 C.M.C.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F . 6 A. M. of California:
BE IT RESOLVED, that Section 221 of the California Masonic
Code be amended to read as follows:
SEC. 221. Appointment and Powers. The Trustees of the
Masonic Homes of California shall be nine in number. The
Deputy Grand Master, Senior Grand Warden and Junior Grand
Warden shall be Trustees ex-officio, the other six Trustees shall
be appointed by successive Grand Masters. The term of appointive Trustees shall be three years from the close of the
Annual Communicatio n of the Grand Lodge. Three appointive
Trustees shall be residents in the vicinity of the Home at Union
City and three shall be residents in the vicinity of the Home at
Covina. 1£ a Trustee shall serve three consecutive terms after
I 948. he shall be ineligible for reappointment until the lapse of
one year.
The Trustees heretofore appointed. and their successors hereafter appointed or elected, shall be the successors of the Trustees
of the Masonic Widows' and Orphans' Home originally appointed under the resolutions of the Grand Lodge adopted in
I 892 and subsequently thereto, and shall have all the powers
given to such Trustees, or their survivors or successors, and shaJI
be vested with all the rights and property by them or any of them
acquired. Said Trustees as successor Trustees are authorized to
tra nsfer and convey to Masonic Homes of California, a non-profit
Corporation, all of the rights and property so acquired and with
which they shall be vested as such successor Trustees.
Respectfully submitted,
L. HAROLD ANDERSON , P.M., No. 346
Referred to Committee on Jurisprudence.

The Committee on Jurisprudence:
The Masonic Home was originally founded by the Trustees of the
Masonic Widows' and Orphans' Home under resolutions of this Grand
Lodge adopted in 1892, and title to the Decoto property was expressly
vested in those trustees as trustees of the Masonic Widows' and
Orphans' Home .
When the present Masonic Homes of California was incorporated
in I 919, the trustees of the Masonic Widows' and Orphans' Home
failed to convey their title to the corporation. Our Masonic law has
always provided that the trustees of the Masonic Homes Corporation
are the successors of the trustees of the trust created by the resolutions
of 1892 and until 1948 vested them with the same powers as the original

PROCEEDING S OF THE
INSURANCE -

PUBLIC LIABILITY AND EXTENDED COVERAGE

In our report las t year attention was called to the new plan with reference to the Public Liability and Extended Coverage Insurance for constituent Lodges providing better protection at more favorable rates.
Under this plan the annual billing to Lodges for insurance coverage was
eliminated and Grand Lodge assumed the premium costs. To accomplish
this, it was necessary to provide an additional per capita of 22¢ in the
1966-1 967 budget to take care of premium cost estimated at approximately $53,000.00 for the first nineteen months under the plan ending
June 30, 1968, to be reduced to a per capita of 14¢ for coverage in subsequent years, assuming premium costs for this type of insurance coverage
will remain stable.
As explained above, the bill for this new insurance was not received
las t year. consequentl y the $53.000.00 estimated premium costs appearing
in the budget was not utilized.
The bill for the insurance now has been received. The total premium
costs amount to just s hort of $95,000.00 and are for the three years beginning July l, 1967. We are pleased to report that the premium is considerably less than was anticipated last year. A part of this reduced cost
is due to the policy being written for a three year period. However. to
obtain this reduced cost, it will be necessary to pay the entire three year
premium in the immediate future. Subject to the approval of this Grand
Lodge. it is the intention to pay the entire premium now. charging $38,000.00 to the expense of the current year and recording the remainder
of $58,000.00 on our books as prepaid insurance to be written off to expense at the rate of $29,000.00 per a nnum for the years beginning July 1,
1968, and 1969, respectively . It is now evident that the 1967 per capita
assessment to carry this insurance program was more than required. It
can likewise be determined that the proposed 1968 and 1969 per capita
assessments of 14¢ will not need to be increased. This is consistent wi th
the per capita costs for the second and third years of the policy projected
in the report of the Finance Committee last year.
CALIFORNIA FREEMA SON

Last year's budget contained a per capita tax of $.35 for the editing.
printing and distribution of the California Freemason to the members of
our Jurisdiction. This Committee has been supplied with estimates of the
various items of expense incurred in the publishing of the magazine. together with estimates of revenue based on the continuance of the $.35
per capita tax. Total projected revenue for 1967-1968 is approxim ately
$84,000.00 and expenses a re estimated a t $80.000.00, which would produ ce a net revenue over expense of $4,000.00. It is our opinion that, in
the publishing of the California Freemason, we are now close to a breakeven point, assuming that revenue and expense can be maintained at their
current levels. Consequent ly, we believe that the present per capita of
$.35 should be continued.

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

265

SALARIES

We again call attention to the fact that. as in recent years. the full
appropriatio n for salaries in the Grand Lodge office has not been used.
This is partly attributable to the Grand Secretary being able to allocate
to various Grand Lodge committees portions of salaries not directly related to the functions of the Gra nd Lodge office. We believe it prudent.
however, to continue the appropriatio n fo r salaries of Grand Lodge office
employees in the same amount as was established last year and are so
recommendi ng in the 1967-1968 budget attached hereto.
GRAND TREASURER 'S R EPORT

The Grand Treasurer's Report was referred to and examined by this
Committee. We find all fi na ncial items in accord with the audit and in
recommendi ng approval of the report we do so with keen appreciation of
the splendid service which our Grand Treasurer continues to render so
unselfishly to this Grand Lodge.
GRAND SECRETARY' S R EPORT

The Grand Secretary and the Assistant Grand Secretary attended
all day meetings on Saturdays in May and in August, 1967, in connection with the 1967- 1968 budget and a number o f special meetings in connection with the study on expenditure of Lodge funds and Grand Lodge
funds. These required a considerable amount of work and time on the
part of the Grand Secretary and members of his staff and your F inance
Committee expresses its appreciation for the cooperation received.
MASONIC HOMES

The Committee on Finance has received a nd examined the Report o f
the Trustees of the Masonic Homes. We can only repeat the commendation extended on every hand to the Trustees and staffs for the efficient
administrati on and operation of our two Masonic Homes. This Committee con curs in the recommenda tion of the Trustees that the present per
capita of $1.50 be continued .
SPECIAL STUDY ON EXPENDITUR ES OF LODGE AND GRAND LODGE FUNDS

The Grand Master commented in his message on the activity of this
Committee in pursuing the mandate given us by Grand Lodge at the 1966
Annual Communica tion - the study on the expenditure of Lodge and
Grand Lodge fu nds.
With the full cooperation of the Grand Secretary and his staff, the
study was commenced at an early date. Questionnai res were sent to all
Grand Jurisdictions in the United S tates and to our own constituent
Lodges. M uch interesting and, in some phases, disturbing data was gathered and summarized in a series of four reports furnished to the Grand
Mas ter, the Grand Secretary and the elective Grand Lodge officers.

266

GRAND LODGE OP CALTPORNIA

PROCEEDIN GS OP THE

These reports, which offered conclusions and recommen dations in the
form of resolutions, were adjudged to require further considerat ion. With
the time necessary for additional study not being available. your Committee on Finance agreed to the request of the Grand M aster that a report
not be presented at this Communi cation and that Grand Lodge be requested to authorize the incoming Grand Master to appoint a special
committee to continue the study and to report to Grand Lodge at the 1968
Annual Comunica tion.

Committe e on Finance are provided for in the proposed budget which

In closing our report last year, we said "we are confident that those
to whom will be entrusted the responsibility for the spending of Grand
Lodge funds will be ever conscious of their obligations to their brethren."
We can repeat those words in closing this report as a statement of
fact and thanks, and further as a challenge.

271

In most w ays we attained our goals in the budget which was pre~
sented last year and we see no reason why the same should not be so for
·
the budget which has just been presented to you.
Your Committee on Finance meets during the year with the elected
line officers of Grand Lodge, the Grand Secretary. the Grand Treasurer
and chairmen of Grand Lodge committees in the preparation of the
annual budget. We are impressed with their devotion to the Fraternity
and the service which they render. Grand Lodge is big business by any
standards. It is complex. It has the fraternal devotion of some 240,000
brethren in California and Hawaii. Obviously the financial side of the
Grand Lodge. as it represents its members. warrants and has the attention
of the brethren.
To continue our service to our brethren, our Lodges and to Masonry
and society as a whole, we off er the following resolution:
RESOLVED: That for the purposes of paying the expenses of
Grand Lodge, a per capita of $3.45 be levied for the fiscal year ending
June 30,1968, divided as follows :

ANNUAL ELECTION
The Grand Master announced that the hour had arrived for the
Annual Election and directed the Grand Secretary to read the sections
of the Constitution applying thereto.
The R. W . Eugene S. Hopp, King Solomon's Seaport Lodge N o.
260. was elected Grand Master.
The R. W. Robert A. Crigler, John Marshall Lodge No. 636, was
elected Deputy Grand Master.
The R. W. Chester R. MacPhee, Golden West Lodge No. 455. was
elected Senior Grand Warden.
The W . Herbert A. Huebner, Wilshire Lodge No. HS. was elected
Junior Grand Warden.

At 12 :30 p.m. Grand Lodge was called off until 2 :00 p.m.

AFTERNOON SESSION -

273

F RIDAY, OCTOBER 13. 1967

At 2 :00 p.m. Grand Lodge was called on, the Grand Master presiding. This session was raised by Brother Henry Korczak, Junior Warden
of Lompoc Lodge No. 262.

INSTALLATION OF OFFICERS
Most Worshipful Ellsworth Meyer, Past Grand Master, acted as
Master of Ceremonies and the officers, elected and appointed, were installed by the retiring Grand Master in accordance with the Ritual.
The Charles Albert Adams lapel pin was transferred from the retiring
to the incumbent Grand Master, and the other chair officers exchanged
the Arthur S. Crites lapel pins.
In the absence of the retiring Grand Chaplain, the Robert B. Watts
lapel pin was presented to the newly installed Grand Chaplain by Most
Worshipful Laurence E. Dayton.
The re tiring Grand Master was invested with the apron of his new
designation by Most Worshipful Ellsworth Meyer. Most Worshipful
Myron E. Smith presented him a Past Grand Master pin from the Trustees of the Masonic H omes. A Past Grand Master Certificate was then
presented to Most Worshipful Laurence E. Dayton by the newly installed Grand Master, Eugene S. Hopp.
On behalf of the members of Grand Lodge. the Grand Secretary
presented a gift for Mrs. Dayton. for which the junor Past Grand Master
expressed gratitude. He spoke of his appreciation for the opportunity of
having served the Fraternity as its Grand Master.
On conclusion ~f the installation ceremony, Most Worshipful Eugene
S. Hopp introduced members of his Lodge who were present. He spoke
with humility and pledged his utmost effort and ability to discharge the
tremendous responsibilities placed upon him through the confidence of
Grand Lodge in electin g him to this position of honor and respect.
At 2: 50 P .M.. all business being completed , Grand Lodge closed in
due form.
